final_answer.key_evidence_summary: Pods inventory in train-ticket shows exactly one business workload missing: ts-assurance-service (all other services 2/2 Running). Complaint side confirms: alert on entry service ts-assurance-service GET /api/v1/assuranceservice/assurances/types returns HTTPError('503 Server Error: Service Unavailable') x11, and CheckServiceConnectivity to ts-assurance-service:18888 (the port its own Service declares) fails on worker-01/02/03. The Service object exists (ClusterIP 10.68.251.254:18888) but has no endpoints; its error log is empty because no pod exists. Workload layer: Deployment ts-assurance-service has spec.replicas: 0 (generation 2, revision 1, status kept at MinimumReplicasAvailable), while GetAppYAML declares replicas: 1 -> the live replica count was scaled to 0. Mechanism event on the events surface: 'ScalingReplicaSet deployment/ts-assurance-service Scaled down replica set ts-assurance-service-88f65755 to 0 from 1' followed by 'SuccessfulDelete replicaset/ts-assurance-service-88f65755 Deleted pod: ts-assurance-service-88f65755-wrfvf', with no later SuccessfulCreate/scale-up for this deployment while every other service was re-created. Containers show a clean 'Killing/Stopping container ts-assurance-service', not OOMKilled or probe-restart churn; no FailedCreate/FailedScheduling/FailedMount/image-pull warnings exist, and resourcequotas returns 'No resources found', excluding the namespace-quota branch.

2. **Then the workload, pruned.** Pods (state + events) → owner chain; for node-scope questions use the pods listing's NODE column.
3. **Take the branch your evidence lands on:**

   - **Never created / missing reference**: the victim's signal first; then the workload state; then the event names the missing object; read the template and the object's own listing. Close a quota case on the namespace quota's used/hard rows (see the L2 quota reading); a missing Service is never a DNS failure.    - **Image pull**: read the failing stage in the message (registry lookup / manifest / token) and classify by that stage (see the L2 image-pull reading); mount/probe errors go to the matching config face.

Train-Ticket has no code surface — do not answer a code class here; read the gateway manifest. This branch also applies when the only "unhealthy" objects are Services absent from the listing while their workloads run and no ResourceQuota object exists — those are background; read the gateway manifest.

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-assurance-service
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ts-assurance-service
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ts-assurance-service
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ts-assurance-service
        image: ghcr.io/sregym/ts-assurance-service:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        env:
        - name: SPRING_MAIN_ALLOW_CIRCULAR_REFERENCES
          value: 'true'
        - name: NODE_IP
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: status.hostIP
        envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: ts-assurance-mysql
        - configMapRef:
            name: nacos
        ports:
        - containerPort: 18888
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 200m
            memory: 350Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 512Mi
        readinessProbe:
          tcpSocket:
            port: 18888
          initialDelaySeconds: 60
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 5
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-assurance-service
spec:
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 18888
  selector:
    app: ts-assurance-service
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-assurance-mysql
type: Opaque
stringData:
  ASSURANCE_MYSQL_HOST: tsdb-mysql-leader
  ASSURANCE_MYSQL_PORT: '3306'
  ASSURANCE_MYSQL_DATABASE: ts
  ASSURANCE_MYSQL_USER: ts
  ASSURANCE_MYSQL_PASSWORD: Ts_123456
